questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How iPods replaced cassette players
Why young people prefer headphones
The invention and success of the Sony Walkman
The history of Japanese pop music
questions.why: They take a nostalgic look back at the birth of the Sony Walkman.

questions.q: Why didn't Georgina answer Neil at the start?
options: She was listening to music on her headphones
She was talking to a friend on her phone
She was busy reading an interesting magazine
She had just arrived late and was out of breath
questions.why: She says she didn't hear him because she was listening to music on her headphones.

questions.q: What gave Akio Morita the idea for the Walkman?
options: Students listening to music on crowded trains
A request from a famous American music journalist
An old cassette player he found in his garage
Teenagers carrying heavy radios on their shoulders
questions.why: He saw Japanese teenagers carrying heavy transistor radios on their shoulders.

questions.q: How did Morita's colleagues react to his idea?
options: They were excited and wanted to start at once
They doubted people would walk around in headphones
They thought it would be too expensive to make
They wanted to sell it only in America at first
questions.why: Andrea Koppen says people were very sceptical that anyone would want to walk around with headphones.

questions.q: Why did Sony give Walkmans to students?
options: Students had asked for free machines
The government paid for it
They had little money for advertising
Students were the only people who liked music
questions.why: Koppen says their advertising budget was very tight, so they decided to give it to students to try.

questions.q: Why does Andrea Koppen mention that Morita put his job on the line?
options: To show he secretly wanted to leave Sony
To show how strongly he believed in the Walkman
To explain why he was later fired by the company
To show that his colleagues fully supported him
questions.why: He said he would resign if it didn't take off, showing how confident he was.

questions.q: What happened to the first 30,000 Walkmans?
options: They all sold out within three months
They were sent back because of faults
They were only sold in the US
Most were given away free
questions.why: Neil says within 3 months the entire first run of 30 thousand Walkmans had sold out.

questions.q: According to Tim Jarman, what did people first expect about the Walkman?
options: It would be popular with all ages
It would replace the radio
It would be too heavy to carry
It would sell only to a small group
questions.why: He says they thought it could be a niche product that might not sell.
